title: Mozi Stops a War on a Tabletop
text:
In the 5th century BC the master craftsman Gongshu Ban built new siege ladders, called cloud ladders, for the powerful state of Chu, which planned to use them against the small state of Song. The philosopher Mozi, who taught universal love and opposed wars of aggression, heard of it. The book that bears his name says he set out at once and walked ten days and ten nights to the Chu capital.

Mozi first argued with Gongshu Ban, then with the king of Chu, pointing out that attacking Song was unjust and that Chu, already rich, gained nothing worth the wrong. Both admitted he was right, but the king said that since Gongshu Ban had built the ladders, he would still take Song.

So Mozi proposed a demonstration. He took off his belt and laid it out as a city wall and used small wooden tablets as machines. Gongshu Ban attacked nine times with nine different devices, and Mozi repelled every attack, with defenses still to spare. Gongshu Ban said he knew a way to beat Mozi but would not say it. Mozi said he knew what it was: to kill him. But, he added, his disciple Qin Guli and three hundred students were already on the walls of Song with his defensive devices. Killing him would change nothing.

The king called off the attack. The text adds that on his way home Mozi passed through Song in the rain and was refused shelter at its gate.
lesson: The best way to stop an attack can be to show, calmly and concretely, that it will fail. Prepare your defenses so that your opponent's decision makes itself.
people: Mozi, Gongshu Ban, King of Chu, Qin Guli
location: Ying, capital of Chu (modern Hubei, China)
